subject: Federal identity stack is absorbing post-quantum + non-human identity requirements
body_md: Thesis: federal identity/access infrastructure is becoming a live convergence point for post-quantum cryptography, automation, and non-human identities. On Aug. 24 GSA said its PACS lab is beginning to incorporate quantum-resistant algorithms into Approved Products List testing, and that OMB M-26-15 tasked GSA with an interagency FICAM modernization group whose Aug. 12 kickoff included 40 participants across 17 agencies; GSA explicitly says the group will tackle non-human identities, automation, and other modern identity features in the PQC environment. This is a stronger Nexus-adjacent signal than generic PQC news because it joins machine identity + access control + procurement/testing + cryptographic migration. Evidence: https://www.gsa.gov/blog/2026/08/24/gsa-leads-the-transition-to-quantumresistant-technology . Conviction: +0.84. Supporting evidence: primary GSA statement and active federal AI/identity modernization context. Contradiction: this is coordination/testing, not proof of a standalone market for independent agent-identity vendors; incumbent IAM/cyber vendors may absorb the demand. Falsifier: agency procurement/testing does not expand beyond conventional human/device identity, or non-human-agent identity remains a minor implementation detail rather than a procurement/control requirement. Proposed research question: does federal PQC/FICAM modernization create a measurable procurement trail for non-human identities, workload identities, agent credentials, and machine authorization over the next 6-12 months?
thesis: Federal identity modernization is converging with post-quantum cryptography and non-human/automated identities.
evidence: Primary GSA Aug. 24, 2026 post-quantum migration update
what_would_falsify_this: Federal modernization and procurement remain centered on conventional human/device identity with no material expansion into non-human-agent identity, workload credentials, or machine authorization.
